properties.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance landing site)
properties.source: NASA named the Mars 2020 landing site on 5 March 2021; published coordinates 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E (≈18°26'N 77°27'E).
properties.why: Documented, real starting point on the crater floor.
properties.limitation: Position precision ~0.01°; one MOLA cell is ~0.008°.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Jezero crater (centre)
properties.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature value (18.38°N, 77.58°E).
properties.why: Reference point used to locate the crater rim.
properties.limitation: Nomenclature centre, not a surveyed point.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Western delta front
properties.source: NASA describes the fan-shaped sedimentary deposit (delta) west of the landing site; position here is an approximate placement from published maps.
properties.why: Deltas form where a river entered a lake; their layered sediments can record past water and environments.
properties.investigate: Layering, grain size and composition of sedimentary rocks exposed at the front.
properties.limitation: APPROXIMATE position — verify against the real MOLA hillshade / HiRISE before presenting. Composition is not measured by MOLA.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Jezero west rim crest (derived)
properties.source: Highest MOLA elevation (-2196 m) sampled along the azimuth from the crater centre through the landing site, between 0.70 and 1.35 crater radii (found at 1.00 R).
properties.why: Impact-crater rims expose material uplifted from depth; a rim position also gives the crew a regional overview.
properties.investigate: Rim-forming rock types and their relation to crater-floor and delta deposits.
properties.limitation: Located from ~463 m topography only; the exact crest and access path need HiRISE-scale data.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

sources.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance landing site)
sources.archive: NASA named the Mars 2020 landing site on 5 March 2021; published coordinates 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E (≈18°26'N 77°27'E).

sources.name: Jezero crater (centre)
sources.archive: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature value (18.38°N, 77.58°E).

sources.name: Western delta front
sources.archive: NASA describes the fan-shaped sedimentary deposit (delta) west of the landing site; position here is an approximate placement from published maps.

sources.name: Jezero west rim crest (derived)
sources.archive: Highest MOLA elevation (-2196 m) sampled along the azimuth from the crater centre through the landing site, between 0.70 and 1.35 crater radii (found at 1.00 R).

region.name: Jezero Crater
region.why: Mars 2020 Perseverance landing region: an ancient crater lake with a preserved delta, giving a clear exploration-and-science narrative and a well-documented start point.

balanced.intent: Trade modeled terrain cost against science proximity.
